collections.name: AFM Magazine
collections.description: A biannual magazine dedicated to fashion, art, and contemporary culture.

collections.name: Apartamento Magazine
collections.description: Today's most influential, inspiring, and honest interiors publication. Exploring the intimate relationship between people and their private spaces since 2008.

collections.name: Black Photographers
collections.description: Photography books by and about Black photographers, exploring their unique perspectives, communities, and contributions to visual culture.

collections.name: BUTT Magazine
collections.description: Legendary independent gay culture and lifestyle magazine known for its distinctive photography, intimate interviews, and honest storytelling. Published from 2001 to 2011, relaunched in 2023.

collections.name: Disaster
collections.description: Photobooks documenting catastrophe, violence, and human tragedy. From Goya's pioneering protest etchings to forensic photography and photojournalism capturing accidents, emergencies, and war.

collections.name: Ephemera
collections.description: Everything in the library tagged Ephemera: the invitations, stickers, postcards and other printed matter of the Ephemera wing, alongside the books and magazines in the art wing that are tagged the same way.

collections.name: Esopus
collections.description: An award-winning arts annual published from 2003 to 2018 by the Esopus Foundation. Each issue featured six long-form contemporary artists' projects alongside personal essays, artist portfolios, visual essays, interviews, poetry, fiction, and a themed audio compilation.

collections.name: Le Petit Voyeur
collections.description: A curated photography magazine featuring exceptional contemporary photographers. Published 2013-2021.

collections.name: Matsuda Fashion Catalogues
collections.description: A collection of rare and influential fashion catalogues from Japanese designer Mitsuhiro Matsuda (published between 1984–1993)

collections.name: Music Photobooks
collections.description: Capturing the energy, aesthetic, and personalities of music scenes and artists through the lens of photography.

collections.name: Purple Magazine
collections.description: An influential French fashion and contemporary culture magazine founded in Paris in 1992 by Elein Fleiss and Olivier Zahm. Purple emerged as a reaction against the superficial glamour of the 1980s, pioneering the "anti-fashion" aesthetic and becoming synonymous with the new realism in fashion photography through collaborators like Juergen Teller, Terry Richardson, Wolfgang Tillmans, and Mario Sorrenti.

collections.name: Queer Culture
collections.description: Queer photography, artists' books, zines, and visual culture from the collection — physique photography and its archives, the West Side piers, Fire Island, drag and nightlife, erotica, appropriation, and queer art history. A growing collection.

collections.name: Record Culture Magazine
collections.description: A magazine celebrating vinyl culture, album art, and the rich history of recorded music.

collections.name: Slanted Magazine
collections.description: A magazine about type, graphic design, and visual culture from around the world.

collections.name: Surveillance Index
collections.description: Photography books about watchers and the watched: photobooks and artists' books, all from the art wing. The index is kept in two editions, and the first was published as a printed guide to one hundred of the books.

collections.name: Surveillance Index Edition Two
collections.description: The second edition of the Surveillance Index: the photography books in the index that are not in Edition One. Edition Two is in production, and this list is incomplete.

collections.name: TISSUE Magazine
collections.description: Independent art and media magazine published from 2011 to 2022, devoted — in its own words — to life and death. Across five print issues, TISSUE mixed photography, nightlife, sexuality, and contemporary culture with a restless, collaged design language. The library holds the complete print run, N°1 through N°5.

collections.name: Toilet Paper
collections.description: An artists' magazine created by Maurizio Cattelan and Pierpaolo Ferrari, featuring provocative photography and surreal imagery. Since 2010, Toilet Paper has combined commercial photography with twisted narrative tableaux, challenging the limits of the contemporary art economy.

collections.name: Useful Photography
collections.description: The complete run of Useful Photography, the influential Dutch annual publication devoted to functional, everyday, and anonymous photography.

collections.name: Collage Collections
collections.description: Exploring the art of assemblage and juxtaposition through photographic collage, cut-and-paste techniques, and related visual works. The works below are part of an actively curated collection of books on collage in the Hudson Street Library.

collections.name: Comme des Garçons Related
collections.description: Exploring the influential and avant-garde world of Rei Kawakubo and Comme des Garçons through books, publications, and related materials.

collections.name: Magazines
collections.description: Independent and art magazines exploring photography, design, and visual culture.

collections.name: One Picture Book Two
collections.description: Nazraeli Press's celebrated series of limited edition photography books. Each volume is limited to 500 numbered copies and includes a removable, signed, original 5x7 inch print by the artist. Featuring work by masters like Daido Moriyama, Michael Kenna, Todd Hido, Alec Soth, and Carrie Mae Weems.

collections.name: Richard Prince
collections.description: A barely comprehensive, not even close to complete collection of publications by and about Richard Prince, the influential American artist known for his appropriation photography, cowboys, jokes, and social media work.

collections.name: Wombat Artist Boxes
collections.description: Limited edition photography portfolios produced by Wombat Paris. Each box contains museum-quality numbered prints on Hahnemühle paper, printed by Processus lab, and unpublished portfolios from contemporary photographers. Hand-assembled, numbered, and stamp-dated in limited editions.
